course.title: Vue.js — Beginner to Advanced
course.description: A visual-first, project-based Vue 3 course that preserves the 152-lesson syllabus from the supplied curriculum PDF and extends it with independent exercises, practical projects, protected knowledge checks, and production-readiness topics.
course.version_scope: Vue 3.x is the primary path. Use the current official create-vue/Vite workflow and the Composition API with Single-File Components and <script setup> for new applications; the Options API remains included for reading existing projects. Feature-specific notes identify requirements such as defineModel() (Vue 3.4+), deferred Teleport (Vue 3.5+), and experimental or runtime-dependent APIs. Official documentation was checked on 2026-10-17; verify package versions again at project setup. Vue 2 reached end of life on 2023-12-31; legacy material is for maintenance/migration. TypeScript is an optional specialization in the curriculum, not a new CodeLeaf source file format.
prerequisites: CSS selectors, layout, and responsive basics
JavaScript variables, functions, objects, arrays, ES modules, promises, and async/await
learning_outcomes: Build interactive interfaces using Vue templates, reactive state, computed values, and watchers.
Create reusable components using props, emitted events, slots, and composables.
Develop multi-page applications with Vue Router and shared state with Pinia.
Integrate APIs and handle forms, validation, loading, empty, and error states.
Test, debug, secure, profile, and optimize Vue applications.
Choose appropriate CSR/SSR/SSG approaches and deploy maintainable applications.

source_correction_log.source_note: The PDF includes defineModel(), deferred Teleport, once-only watchers, v-memo, and Suspense-related material.
source_correction_log.verification: Official Vue API/tooling guides distinguish version-specific and experimental capabilities; the precise runtime requirements should be checked for each project.
source_correction_log.decision: Kept the scope, added caution notes where applicable, and marked experimental/runtime-dependent usage for verification before production.

source_correction_log.topic: Vue and Vue CLI setup recommendations
source_correction_log.source_note: The PDF recommends create-vue with Vite for new projects and treats Vue CLI as legacy/maintenance tooling.
source_correction_log.verification: Matches current Vue tooling guidance reviewed on 2026-10-17.
source_correction_log.decision: Retained Vite/create-vue for new projects and preserved legacy tooling as migration material.

source_correction_log.source_note: The PDF says Vue 2 reached end of support on December 31, 2023.
source_correction_log.verification: The Vue project’s official EOL notice confirms that date.
source_correction_log.decision: Retained the topic as legacy maintenance guidance, not as a recommended baseline for new apps.

source_correction_log.source_note: The PDF includes a TypeScript specialization.
source_correction_log.verification: This CodeLeaf project uses JavaScript/JSX and the task explicitly prohibits .ts/.tsx files.
source_correction_log.decision: Included TypeScript as optional reference-only course content; no .ts/.tsx source files or TypeScript project dependencies were added.

source_correction_log.source_note: The PDF pages include a Vue logo graphic, small third-party/source labels, and project UI screenshots.
source_correction_log.decision: Inspected the 34-page PDF and visual contact sheet. Did not reuse external branding or screenshots; generated original SVG learning diagrams with captions and alt text.

source_correction_log.source_note: The PDF is a curriculum outline, not a reviewed lesson manuscript.
source_correction_log.decision: All course/module/lesson/exercise/assessment/project content remains draft until reviewed. No course is published by this patch.

learning_roadmap.title: Foundation
learning_roadmap.goal: Understand Vue, set up Vite projects, master templates/directives, and learn reactivity.

learning_roadmap.title: Components and reusable UI
learning_roadmap.goal: Build forms, well-designed components, lifecycle cleanup, styling, and transitions.

learning_roadmap.title: Real applications
learning_roadmap.goal: Compose reusable logic, navigate with Router, integrate API data, and share state through Pinia.

learning_roadmap.title: Advanced development
learning_roadmap.goal: Study advanced rendering, optional TypeScript, testing, accessibility/security, and measured optimization.
learning_roadmap.note: Module 15 is optional specialization and should not block the JavaScript-first path.

learning_roadmap.title: Professional delivery
learning_roadmap.goal: Understand SSR/Nuxt, deployment, monitoring, collaboration, legacy migration, and the capstone.

prerequisite_map.reason: Reactive state assumes familiarity with templates and directives.
Component props/events are easier to model after reactive state.
Composables reuse reactive behavior and component-context APIs.
Routing organizes component views across URLs.
API workflows use asynchronous JavaScript and cleanup patterns.
Shared stores extend the same state model across components.
Component tests exercise props, events, and rendered output.
SSR and Nuxt build on component, routing, and data-fetching concepts.

core_vs_optional.description: Core Vue fundamentals and ecosystem application skills.
Advanced components, testing, inclusive/security engineering, performance, production delivery, and professional practices.
TypeScript and large-scale code organization; optional alongside the JavaScript-first path.
Retained for reading and modernizing existing applications.
Check official docs and runtime versions before relying on version-specific behavior in production.
